findings.title: Duplicate `self.downsize` definition silently overrides the 4-argument version
findings.body: `self.downsize` is now defined twice: at line 145 as `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` and again at line 149 as `(from, to, dimensions, opts)`. Ruby keeps only the later definition, so the first is dead code and any caller using the `max_width, max_height` form (the original API) now gets a wrong argument mapping: `max_height` lands in `opts` and the call fails or behaves incorrectly. Only the 3-argument form used by uploads_controller works. Remove one definition and keep a single signature.

findings.title: Animated downsize passes a percentage to gifsicle --resize-fit
findings.body: The controller calls `downsize(..., "80%", allow_animation: ...)`. For GIFs, `optimize` routes to `downsize_instructions_animated`, which calls `resize_instructions_animated` and emits `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`. gifsicle's `--resize-fit` expects a WxH geometry, not a percentage, so the resize fails. `convert_with` returns false, the controller ignores that, and animated GIFs over the limit are never reduced. Animated GIFs need a separate code path or an explicit scale that gifsicle accepts.

findings.title: Downsize loop ignores failure and retries the same conversion up to 5 times
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns false when conversion fails (`convert_with` swallows errors), but the loop doesn't check the return value. A failed conversion leaves the file unchanged, so the loop runs all five attempts on identical input, wasting time, and then proceeds to `Upload.create_for` with an oversized file. The loop should stop on failure, and the oversized case should be reported to the user rather than silently accepted. Also, `tempfile.size` may be stale if the tool replaces the file rather than rewriting it in place, so the loop condition needs verification.

findings.title: Client-side size limit now hardcoded to 10MB, removing the per-type site setting
findings.body: The `max_' + type + '_size_kb` site setting lookup was replaced with a hardcoded `10 * 1024`. Admins who configured `max_image_size_kb` or `max_attachment_size_kb` will see their settings ignored in the browser, which is a regression. The server still enforces its own limits, so the client now disagrees with the configured policy.

findings.title: Client rejects files over 10MB before the server can downsize them
findings.body: The feature is meant to accept large images and shrink them server-side, but this client check rejects any file larger than 10MB before upload. Users uploading large images will still see the error, so the feature is ineffective from the UI. The check needs to allow images above the limit (or skip it for images) to match the server behavior.

findings.title: HTTP 413 message now hardcodes 10MB instead of the configured image limit
findings.body: The 413 branch previously showed `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`. It now always displays 10 MB, so the error text can disagree with the actual configured limit that the server enforces.

findings.title: API URL download limit changed from the site setting to a hardcoded 10MB
findings.body: The remote URL download cap was switched from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a fixed `10.megabytes`. This changes the API contract: admins who lowered the image size setting no longer constrain downloads, and the 10MB cap is not configurable.

findings.title: No tests for the new large-image downsize path
findings.body: The change adds automatic downsizing in the upload controller, changes the `OptimizedImage` method signatures, and changes client validation, but the PR includes no specs. Nothing covers the loop, its failure handling, animated GIFs, or the duplicate `downsize` definition.

findings.title: PR description is not meaningful
findings.body: The description is only 'Test 1'. It does not explain the behavior change, the removal of the site-setting-based limits, or the 10MB hardcoding, so reviewers cannot assess the intent.
